title: packet_demand_units u32 wrap guard bounds bandwidth_demand only — packet_bandwidth (the other operand) is validated >0 with no upper bound
evidence: core/flow.odin:601: `return u32(demand) * u32(cat.balance.packet_bandwidth)`. core/catalog.odin:630-635: `// ... bound it at load so the product can never wrap (an authoring-time // silent wrap would corrupt the AD-3(c) serialization term; 4096 x // 800 = 3.3M << 2^32, and no real frame is 4096 jumbo-frames wide). if bw > 4096 { return {"packet_types.json", pt.id, "bandwidth_demand must be 1..4096 (the u32 demand-total bound)"} }`. core/catalog.odin:863-866: `b.packet_bandwidth = jint(obj, "packet_bandwidth", 30) if b.packet_bandwidth <= 0 { return {"balance.json", "packet_bandwidth", "must be > 0 ..."} }`
detail: A catalog passing all validation (demand 4096, packet_bandwidth 1048576 — only `<= 0` is rejected) wraps the u32 product; at exactly 2^32 it wraps to 0, serve_bundle_lane's need=0 skips the packet forever — never served, never dropped.
recommended_fix: Complete the guard at load: reject packet_bandwidth > 2^32/4096 (1048576), or widen the multiply to u64 in packet_demand_units (and transit_ticks' demand_units+capacity-1 addition).
